name: Blazebelly Ant
reason: The source creature 'Explosive Flame Ant' was renamed 'Blazebelly Ant' to give the fire-themed insect a punchier, more evocative Western fantasy name.
description: A fire-aligned insect monster fought during the divine-tree trial arc (Ep 1251, source ch ~1231). Its carapace offers weak defense, and the party cuts the ants down with ease.

name: Trinity Realm
reason: The source realm 'Three Pure Realms' was localized as 'Trinity Realm', preserving the 'three' concept in a single natural English word.
description: An Upper Realm territory of the alliance, entered via an ascending pool (Ep 1252). It is governed by a Realm Master who is also the Holy Lord of the Jadeheart Sanctuary (source: Jade Pure Holy Land), and it houses the elite Lucent Hall.

name: Four Great Clans
reason: The source collective 'four great families' was localized as 'Four Great Clans' for the Western fantasy register.
description: The four preeminent family powers of the late universe-level arc; in the source any one of them far exceeds an ordinary tenth-rank Holy Land in power. Many of the elite warriors seen in Ep 1265 belong to them.

name: Illusive Fog
reason: The source technique 'Rebirth Illusory Fog' was shortened and localized as 'Illusive Fog'.
description: A concealing fog Zane's side uses for cover during the late Illusion Battlefield fighting (Eps 1276-1277); at least one enemy proves able to see through it, just as Zane's eyes can pierce some Dark Laws.

name: Forceful Crystal Armor
reason: The source defensive technique 'Astral Crystal Saint Body' was localized as 'Forceful Crystal Armor', recasting the body-forging term as armor for clarity.
description: A crystalline defensive technique formed by Damon (source counterpart: Big Dream's Astral Crystal Saint Body). Coleman times his hook attack to the instant the armor forms (Ep 1277).

name: Otherworldly Swordsman
reason: 'Otherworldly Swordsman' is the famous title of the independent sword genius Larkin (source: Dugu Jian Xiaoxiao), so mentions fold into his character entry.
description: Title of Larkin, the only independent warrior ever to reach Ace Talent rank; he severs even the Heavenly Laws of the Hall of Causality with his sword (Eps 1280-1282, source: Dugu Jian Xiaoxiao in the Karma Hall).

name: Lucent Hall
reason: The source 'Qingling Martial Hall', core training ground of the Jade Pure Sacred Ground, was renamed 'Lucent Hall' to fit the Western fantasy register.
description: The elite training hall of the Jadeheart Sanctuary in the Trinity Realm, reserved for the most talented disciples. It stands nearly empty while the top Soul Sea Realm warriors are away competing in the Illusion Battlefield (Eps 1284-1285).

name: Upper World Tia
issues: Extraction artifact: taken from sentences like 'she'd just arrived in the Upper World, Tia had heard...' (Ep 963), conflating the location 'Upper World' with the character 'Tia'.
reason: Not a real entity; a sentence-boundary fragment joining 'Upper World' and 'Tia', each already covered by its own entry.

name: Flame Bees
reason: A fire-creature species from the lava-region arc; no confident source counterpart was identified in the aligned chapters.
description: Fire-aligned bee creatures mentioned during the lava-lake region of the Karma Hall arc (Ep 1295).

name: Floating Feather Technique
reason: The source's 'Floating Technique' was localized as 'Floating Feather Technique', adding 'Feather' to make the levitation imagery more vivid.
description: A rare movement technique for drifting weightlessly; a mysterious woman is startled that Zane knows it too (Ep 1299, mirroring source ch 1279).

name: Godly Way of Snow
reason: The source 'Snow Seal Divine Dao' was localized as 'Godly Way of Snow', replacing the Daoist term 'Divine Dao' with 'Godly Way' per the show's convention.
description: A snow-aspected Divine Way whose inheritor must be innately compatible with it; its guardian woman rejects incompatible candidates, and Zane is eager to learn what compatibility requires (Eps 1299-1300, source ch 1280).

name: Domineering Divine Path
reason: The source term 'domineering Divine Path' was carried over nearly verbatim, as it already reads naturally in English.
description: A Divine Path forged from untamed, commanding willpower; its creator (source: the True God Mo Chen) mastered it through his wild, overbearing nature (Eps 1301-1302).

name: Path of Sealed Emotion
reason: The source 'Emotion-Severing Divine Dao' (also rendered 'Severing of Emotions Divine Dao') was localized as 'Path of Sealed Emotion' to fit the show's 'Path/Way' naming for Divine Daos.
description: A Divine Way achieved by cutting off all emotion, walked in the past by the sword emperor figure of the Emperor's Corridor arc (Ep 1302; source: Chen Huang Yijian's Emotion-Severing Divine Dao).

name: Sunrest Wood
reason: The source's Western primordial tree, the 'Ruo Wood' (the mythic tree where the sun sets), was localized as 'Sunrest Wood', translating the myth rather than the pinyin.
description: The western one of the four primordial divine trees anchoring the cardinal directions (Ep 1310; source ch 1290's Western Ruo Wood). Like the Aetherwood, it has stood since the beginning of the universe.

name: Aetherwood
reason: The source's Southern Dipper 'Seeker Wood' was localized as 'Aetherwood', a cleaner mystical coinage for the Western fantasy setting.
description: The southern one of the four primordial divine trees (Ep 1310; source ch 1290's Southern Dipper Seeker Wood). It has existed since the birth of the universe and, in the source, is noted for extremely fast reproduction.

name: Saint-Killing Spear Slade
issues: Extraction artifact conflating two entities that appear adjacent in Eps 1313-1316: the weapon 'Saint-Killing Spear' (source: Holy Spear of Massacre, the Fiend clan's number one weapon) and its wielder 'Slade' (source: Ming Dao).
reason: Not a real entity; the weapon and its wielder are separate entities with their own entries.

name: Umbral Plane
reason: A shadow-dimension name coined for the adaptation's register; no confident source term was identified in the aligned chapters.
description: A shadow dimension from which a Shadow Creature launches its hook attacks; the creature itself cannot leave its own plane (Eps 999-1000).

name: Astral Body
reason: A body-forging concept from the source narrative; the exact source term was not identified in the aligned chapters.
description: A constructed body that Zane hopes to help forge for the Cobalt Dragon, a feat acknowledged to be no small undertaking (Ep 1005).

name: Vital Spirit
reason: The source term 'Vital Spirit' was carried over unchanged, as it already suits the Western fantasy register.
description: A reserve of explosive power buried deep in a warrior's body that can erupt to the surface in battle, carrying Law power such as the Law of Wind (Eps 550, 1015). The source uses the identical term for the same burst-release phenomenon.

name: Low Grade-Three Divine-Class
reason: The source weapon grade 'Secondary Grade Three Divine Artifact' was localized as 'Low Grade-Three Divine-Class' to systematize the divine-weapon tier naming.
description: A tier within the divine-weapon grading system, one grade above Zane's own weapon at the time; the Emerald weapon shown in Ep 1034 is of this class.

name: Sword Painting
reason: The source technique 'Sword Painting the Landscape' (Sima Yulong's signature art) was shortened to 'Sword Painting' for the adaptation.
description: Fenton Summers' signature sword art (source: Sima Yulong's 'Sword Painting the Landscape'), a seamless fusion of Metal Law and Wind Law that conjures a luminous painting; its light vanishes only if the painted king is slain (Eps 1037-1038, 1076).

name: Psychean Sanctum
reason: The source power 'Spiritual Martial Sanctuary' (Lingwu Holy Land), ruling holy land of the Spiritual World, was localized as 'Psychean Sanctum'.
description: The dominant holy-land power of the Spiritual World arc, led by a Holy Lord; Zane's allies muse that with his power they might even unseat the Sanctum itself (Eps 1039-1040).

name: Celestial Mouse
reason: The source god beast 'Heavenly Rat' (also rendered 'Heavenly Mouse') was localized as 'Celestial Mouse', softening 'Rat' for Western audiences.
description: A divine beast of the setting; in the source it is counted among the god beasts and famed as one of the fastest. In the show, the softest down from a Celestial Mouse's back is used for luxurious plumes (Eps 564, 1040).

name: Deputy Palace Master
reason: The source rank 'Vice Palace Lord' was localized as 'Deputy Palace Master', matching the show's 'Palace Master' terminology.
description: A senior leadership rank in the heavenly-palace powers of the Mist Palace arc, standing just below the Palace Master (Eps 1044, 1061; source: Vice Palace Lord, chs 1022-1043).

name: Hall of True Mysteries
reason: The source's 'Profound Hall' (Xuan hall) was localized as 'Hall of True Mysteries', expanding the terse Chinese 'Profound' into an evocative English name.
description: A hall within the Mist Palace complex; a humiliated rival glares at Zane and his sword, then spins on his heel and stomps into it (Ep 1053, mirroring source ch 1030).

name: Argent Fighting Soul
reason: The source's 'Silver Soul Realm' stage was localized as 'Argent Fighting Soul', tying the silver tier to the show's 'Fighting Soul Realm' terminology.
description: A silver tier of the Fighting Soul Realm, reached when a soul grows strong enough to aid its body directly in combat. Lavender's Argent Fighting Soul can handle two Spirit Supreme Realm warriors even as a disembodied soul (Eps 1053, 1072).

name: Lavender the Queen of Slaughter
reason: 'Queen of Slaughter' is an epithet of Lavender (source: Xun, the woman whose soul hides within the sword spirit); mentions fold into her character entry.
description: Epithet form of Lavender, the shattered-souled woman Zane shelters and restores; her king statue and surviving soul sliver make her a threat the Queen of Punishment is desperate to extinguish (Eps 1053-1055).

name: Jared
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Jared', a common masculine name fitting a minor warrior antagonist.
description: A skilled warrior of the Mist Palace arc whom Zane sent flying with a single punch; the memory of his defeat deters Caleb from pressing a quarrel over Zane's sword (Ep 1057).

name: Nether God Mind Method
reason: The source's 'Serene Spirit Mental Cultivation Method' was localized as 'Nether God Mind Method', matching the show's 'Nether God' rendering of the technique family.
description: The soul-cultivation method behind Zane's Nether God Shadows (source: the method that produces Serene Spirit Shadows), allowing the practitioner to project multiple battle shadows at once at heavy soul-power cost (Eps 1060, 1092).

name: Tiger’s Roar Token
reason: The source item 'Tiger's Roar Command' was localized as 'Tiger's Roar Token', aligning with the show's 'Token' naming for challenge items.
description: A challenge token, a stronger variant of the ordinary Roar Token; a brash newcomer used one to challenge every warrior in the Mist Palace, annoying more than a few of them (Eps 1061, 1064).

name: Justin
reason: Short form of 'Justin Fields', the Cloudswallow Hall prodigy; episodes use the full name, so mentions fold into that entry.
description: Short-form mentions of Justin Fields, a Cloudswallow Hall genius and protégé of a Mist Palace vice leader, said to have unlocked a five-petal (later likely seven-petal) lotus (Ep 1063).

name: Soul Split Spell
reason: Names the soul-dividing art behind the source Palace Master Yun Luo's scattered clones; the exact source term is not attested in the evidence.
description: A spell by which a powerful woman scattered fragments of her soul across the continent while her true self remained in the highest echelons of the upper world (Eps 681, 1063); it corresponds to the soul clones of the source's Palace Master Yun Luo.

name: Empyreans
reason: Plural generic already covered by the singular entity 'Empyrean' (source: Empyrean, chs 652-1303); the plural mentions belong to that entry.

name: Space Erasing Hand
reason: A space-annihilating palm technique named for the adaptation's register; no confident source term was identified in the aligned chapters.
description: A space-erasing palm technique that headlines Ep 1094, wielded by an attacker so overwhelmingly powerful that the warriors' counterattacks prove useless.

name: Lady Darkmere's and Raven
issues: Extraction artifact conjoining two separate characters from a possessive-coordination phrase in Ep 454: Lady Darkmere (leader of Bloodwood Cliff) and Raven (leader of the Black Mountain Order).
reason: Not a real entity; both characters have their own entries.

name: Upper World the Cobalt Dragon
issues: Extraction artifact conflating the location 'Upper World' with 'the Cobalt Dragon' from adjacent words in Eps 476 and 651; each is already covered by its own entry.
reason: Not a real entity; a sentence fragment joining two existing entities.

name: Quincy
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Quincy' for a minor tournament fighter; no confident source counterpart was identified among the candidates.
description: An independent fighter at early Soul Realm who defeated Raven of the Black Mountain Order by the narrowest margin after an evenly matched tournament bout of nearly half an hour (Ep 487).
